items.note: It gives one clear recommendation: stay on Postgres with pgvector. It also says when to switch to Qdrant.
It works out the size of 5M × 1536-dim vectors and projects growth at 1M per quarter, up to 11M. It then uses that for RAM and cost estimates and covers both with halfvec.

The baseline is built around the existing RDS Postgres: instance classes, Multi-AZ and no migration. It doesn't confirm that pgvector 0.8 runs on RDS PG16, but it still treats the existing setup as the starting point.

Each option's estimated cost is compared to $500 per month, and it notes where pgvector would go over budget as data grows. Several figures are unverified estimates, but the budget is applied throughout.

Tenant_id filtering gets a lot of attention: post-filter recall loss, iterative scans, partitioning, partial indexes, exact scans for small tenants, Qdrant's is_tenant index and Pinecone namespaces. It is also a column in the table.
The wide scan looks at more options, but the final comparison table has exactly 4: pgvector, Qdrant, Pinecone and S3 Vectors.
It includes a comparison table and one clear recommendation.

It had no web access, so none of the sources were confirmed to be from the last 12 months. Several are marked [older] and the rest 'date unverified'. It is open about this, but the requirement isn't met.
It follows the requested approach: a wide scan of 9 options, then a ranking, then a deep dive on the top 2 (pgvector and Qdrant).
